The digital data passes through IC5a and IC5c for buffering, and then to the SYNC detector and register...
The RC circuit connected to the RESET input resets the SYNC detector if the digital data has a 0 degree phase shift, or is 1100.
If the digital data is 0011, 0110 or 1001 the circuit is not reset and the output of IC6a remains HIGH.
This means no SYNC cycle is present. The HIGH output of IC6a is used in the rest of the circuit to indicate that the SYNC cycle was not received.
If the digital input is 0111, a SYNC cycle, the output of IC6a is LOW...
The LOW output of IC6a is used in the rest of the circuit to indicate that a SYNC cycle was received.

Remember that in the process of converting the QPSK analog signal to digital data, only the last two bits of the four are used to indicate the wave's phase. Therefore only the Q2 and Q3 outputs of IC7 are used.
The Q2 and Q3 outputs are routed to IC8, which converts the data to serial form by alternately reading first one bit and then the other.

IC9 inverts the data to the original polarity. The output is the digital information that was applied to the PSK/QPSK modulator.
Finally, IC3b is the counter that develops the LOAD signal to the register.
